Happy path: a normally-rendering organisation
=============================================

Summary: In Review, an agent produces a complete piece of work and a person checks and approves it. In Product spec, Tech spec and CI/CD, a person does the work and an assistant helps on request. Code has nothing established yet and is moving toward a way of working where an agent produces a complete piece of work and a person checks and approves it. Nothing could be measured in Plan, Test & QA and Operate.

What we cannot see:
- (ours) Some of the numbers behind parts of the map could not be read.
- (ours) Design documents are not compared with the code they describe.
- (ours) Whether a check or build passed is not read.
- (ours) Deploy and rollback events are not read.
- (ours) Incident and alert events are not read.
- (ours) Whether agents coordinate this organisation's work under its own policies, the highest level on the map, is not read.

Constraints and the moves that clear them:
- Recorded review reaches under half of AI-written pull requests.
  Recorded review reaches 22% of AI-written pull requests (40 of 180 merged in the last 90 days). Review done before a pull request opens is never recorded, so treat this as a floor.
  Move: Make recorded review the gate for AI-written pull requests.
  Once more than half of your AI-written pull requests carry a recorded review, review becomes the usual gate for AI-written code. That is about 101 more reviewed pull requests at today's volume, since each one also adds to the total.
- Few AI-written pull requests merge with little back-and-forth.
  Of the 180 AI-written pull requests merged in the last 90 days, 35 needed little back-and-forth before merging.
  Move: Let agents take more pull requests to merge with little back-and-forth.
  Once more than one in five of these pull requests work this way, your map counts it as a practice your team is adopting. That is about 2 more such pull requests at today's volume.
- A review bot clears few changes without a person re-reading them.
  Your review bot looked at 1,507 merged pull requests. 210 of them merged on the bot's review alone.
  Move: Let your review bot approve low-risk pull requests on its own.
  Once more than one in five of these pull requests work this way, your map counts it as a practice your team is adopting. That is about 115 more bot-cleared pull requests at today's volume.
- Few of your people use an assistant while running releases.
  Across your deployment work, this practice is still rare: a person runs the release and asks the assistant about it. In the last 90 days, 1 of 20 people followed it.
  Move: Have an assistant answer questions while your people run releases.
  Once more than one in five of these people work this way, your map counts it as a practice your team is adopting. That is about 4 more people.
